body:
**Want.** A web work displays on the Art Computer as its own page, the way a browser shows it. Today the player shows it inside a frame, and some artists' sites refuse to be framed. Leander Herzog's holz (`https://leanderherzog.ch/2026/holz/`) is one: `ff-cli display` printed "Displaying" and the screen showed a broken-file icon (feral-file/ff-player#302).

**Decided.**
- We respect the artist's headers. We never strip them or work around them.
- The Art Computer identifies the work by itself. The phone app is a controller, not a dependency.
- The label names the exhibition.
- A curator's card shows only where the curator wrote one.

**Not decided.** The label's form, which is with B&F this week, and whether we keep the cross-fade (#3293).

**Done when.**
- holz displays on an FF1 from `ff-cli display`.
- Living Code plus holz runs overnight with every work displayed.
- A work that can't load is reported as not displayed, on the device and to the sender.

**What exists.** A prototype is running on Office. It made 52 and then 67 changes of work on 11/16 with none refused, and memory stayed steady. The record lists what it doesn't cover (images and video, offline, scaling, setup, status to the app), with the three prototype files: [raw/sessions/2026-11-16-display-prototype.md](https://github.com/feral-file/canon/blob/main/raw/sessions/2026-11-16-display-prototype.md).

comments.body:
@moskovich, I think this investigation gives us a reason to expand the scope beyond replacing the iframe with browser tabs. I propose a scoped native rewrite of the player to replace the current ff-player web application.

We started using Chromium and CDP very early, while prototyping the system. That approach helped us build and ship the Art Computer, but surviving until today does not mean it fits everything we now need. We are asking it to handle artwork lifecycle, phone-controlled keyboard and cursor input, labels, transitions, offline playback, and recovery. This card exposes one architectural limit; moving to tabs addresses framing, but we still need to decide who owns those other responsibilities.

The native application should own playback state, input, cursor and label presentation, and recovery. The artwork should run as its own page, at its own address, with its security policies intact. The phone remains a controller, and a broken artwork must not take away our ability to control the device or explain what failed.

This also connects to our longer-term goal: the hardware and software should remain usable and maintainable even if Feral File disappears. Open-source Chromium gives us an important foundation, but our own runtime needs a clear, documented interface that someone else can understand, build, repair, and carry forward. CDP is an official interface, but depending on its evolving protocol for core product behavior creates an ongoing compatibility obligation. We should deliberately choose where that obligation belongs.

I also think we should reconsider what is feasible with agentic coding now. The models and tools have improved quickly. I would like us to give the strongest available model a clearly scoped, time-boxed trial and see how far we can get, rather than dismissing the direction based on what this work would have cost before. That is a reason to run the experiment, not to lower the quality bar.

For the trial, I suggest we agree on a fixed deadline and test one complete path on an FF1:

- Display holz and Living Code as top-level works, respecting artist headers.
- Support phone cursor movement, clicks, dragging, scrolling, and keyboard input, with device-owned cursor and labels.
- Report failures honestly to the screen and sender, and recover from renderer or browser failure without losing playback state.
- Exercise mixed media and offline restart, then run the overnight playback test already required by this card.

The trial should also document how the runtime is built, installed, and updated. Demonstrate updating its browser engine dependency with upstream security patches so maintenance is part of the evaluation from the beginning.

The trial should focus on whether a native player gives us a better foundation than continuing to extend the current ff-player. At the deadline, we review working behavior, remaining gaps, and maintenance cost, then decide whether to continue, narrow the approach, or stop. My proposal is to give a purpose-built native player a serious, bounded attempt before investing further in the current architecture.

title: Display each work as its own page, at its own address
